question: Which filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose for this issue: a `tools.fs` allow/deny PathGuard policy, a `tools.fs.roots` access-mode policy, or a narrower workspace-only plus separate exec-deny design?
rationale: The choice defines a public config surface and a security boundary, and the current open implementation candidates differ on compatibility, exec scope, media coverage, and operator semantics.

options.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
options.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require deny-wins normalized path tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging any implementation path.

options.title: Split exec into a separate boundary
options.body: Land a file-tool-only policy only if docs and tracking clearly state shell-mediated filesystem access remains a separate security issue.

options.title: Defer to OS/container isolation
options.body: Close or downgrade the config request only if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own host path ACLs beyond workspaceOnly and sandbox backends.

recommendation.title: Settle one `tools.fs` path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose one canonical config shape, require deny-wins normalized path tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging any implementation path.
